Prose block

Source: R/prose-block.R
new_prose_block.Rd

Text that can compute. The block holds markdown, edited as it reads (bold as bold, no syntax to learn), and R inside it the way Quarto writes inline code: `r nrow(data)`. Typing `r and a space in the editor opens a small code field that suggests the inputs, their columns and a few common functions; Enter computes it, and the text shows the value, marked with a dotted underline. Pointing at a value shows its code, a click edits it.

Usage

new_prose_block(text = character(), ...)

Arguments

text

Markdown string, with inline R as `r expr`.

...

Forwarded to blockr.core::new_block().

Value

A prose_block (also a text_block).

Details

The markdown with its code is the block's setting, in its control. Its result is the markdown with the values written in, which the next block takes as text (a report, a slide). Because the code is Quarto's own inline code, the same text runs in a Quarto document where the inputs are objects of the same names.

An expression that fails marks its value in the editor; in the result it stops the block with the error.

Values refresh eagerly as you type, outside the DAG. The text itself commits on blur or Ctrl+Enter, never on a keystroke, so typing does not recompute the blocks downstream.

Who can run code

Whoever can edit the text can run R code on the server, as with the script block. The code runs in a fresh environment whose parent is the global environment, so <<- and assign(..., envir = globalenv()) write to a place that all sessions of the app share.

Inputs

The block takes any number of inputs, including none, named as in new_script_block():

  • The first link into the block is data.

  • Every further link is read by its link name, or as .arg2, .arg3, ... when the link has none.

  • With no input connected the text is plain text, or computes with values that need no input.

On export each input the text uses is replaced by the id of the upstream block.

Examples

if (interactive()) {
  library(blockr.core)
  serve(
    new_board(
      blocks = list(
        data = new_dataset_block("iris", "datasets"),
        note = new_prose_block("## Iris\n\nThere are **`r nrow(data)`** rows.")
      ),
      links = links(from = "data", to = "note", input = "data")
    )
  )
}
